scenes.title: Cold open
narration: This is Affranchi, the dance of the free people of color.
Explore its history from the colonial era to the present.

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Affranchi originated in colonial Saint-Domingue among free people of color called affranchis, meaning manumitted.
Initially, the term described free people of mixed French-African descent.
After the Haitian Revolution, it referred to the light-skinned elite known as the Mulatto ascendancy.
on_screen: Map: Haiti · Caribbean
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Affranchi was performed for colonial entertainment by Europeans and affranchis, and sometimes involved enslaved people dancing for guests.
It is associated with African-descended Kings and Queens and carries regal connotations.
Today, it is performed at Haitian country festivals, Vodou services, and as a tourist attraction.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The National Troupe of Haiti played a key role in reviving Affranchi in the 1950s.
The dance influenced the tumba francesa in Cuba, which shares the African improvisation element but uses drums instead of strings and woodwinds.

Affranchi is a Haitian folk dance with roots in colonial free people of color culture, blending French formal dance figures with African improvisation, and influencing diaspora dances like Cuba's tumba francesa.

music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Affranchi (Haiti). Instruments: string instruments, woodwind instruments. Mood: regal, formal, improvisational. It should sound like this: Music features string and woodwind instruments, supporting formal French-style figures and African improvisation without drum rhythms. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.
